meta.title: Hungarian A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hungarian → English (see the Hungarian, recall the meaning) and English → Hungarian (see an English meaning, recall the Hungarian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words of Hungarian for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Hungarian has examinations at these levels, but no graded word list for any of them was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 328 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, introducing yourself, family, numbers, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the articles, pronouns, question words, postpositions and particles every sentence is built out of — and the other 172 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hungarian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Hungarian dictionaries give them, in the third person singular (eszik "eats", lát "sees"), the form the endings are built on. The 161 nouns show their plural, their accusative and their "his, her" form, the part vowel harmony makes hard to guess (ló, lovak, lovat, lova), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 91 verbs show their "I" form, their past and their infinitive (eszik, eszem, evett, enni), and behind the fold the present in both conjugations — the definite one is used when the object is definite (látok egy házat, "I see a house"; látom a házat, "I see the house") — the past, the conditional and the imperative by person. The Hungarian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Every word carries three real example sentences, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
